description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 on geometry problems and tree width for rollout search, comparing the performance of two models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis represents the number of child nodes, or tree width, with a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, marked at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents Accuracy@1 in percentage, with a linear scale from 15 to 35, marked at intervals of 5. The GPT-4o line is depicted in dark blue with a solid line style and circle markers, starting at 24.4% accuracy at a tree width of 1, increasing to 34.4% at a tree width of 5, and then decreasing to 31.1% at a tree width of 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet line is shown in light blue with a solid line style and cross markers, beginning at 26.7% accuracy at a tree width of 1, remaining relatively stable at 27.8% at a tree width of 3, and then declining to 20.0% at a tree width of 7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
